strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves the approved-candidate active replacement boundary from caller-supplied target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe journey continuation.

Continues an admitted journey through existing headless.run.drive/headless.run.advance authority across the first active Mode Pack mutation boundary after approval while preserving explicit stop-boundary behavior.
Keeps replacement eligibility, target derivation, approval/provenance/fetch/current-active binding, replay, and denial in the Rust runtime rather than the VSIX or headless caller.

Binds replacement route resume to selected-candidate approval, provenance-verification, fetch, registry-selection, and current-active evidence so a headless caller can recover from bounded runtime state.
Consumes approved Mode Pack candidate evidence through existing active replacement authority while preserving bounded checkpoint and ledger metadata.
Returns bounded replacement route-resume metadata with source checkpoint fingerprint, derived target class, result continuation, post-route progress, replay state, and next action.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive can accept one explicitly authorized journey_route_resume envelope and derive modepack_selected_approved_candidate_replacement_target from persisted approval, provenance, fetch, registry-selection, and current active Mode Pack evidence without caller-supplied replacement target assembly.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.2 derives fetch, M50.3 derives provenance verification, and M50.4 derives approval. Existing active replacement still requires the caller to inspect bounded checkpoints and construct a trusted replacement target outside Rust-owned journey execution.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller can reach approved-candidate evidence but still cannot mutate the active Mode Pack in the Golden Journey without external glue that reconstructs replacement identity and replay state.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.4 approval route resume, M50.3 provenance route resume, and M50.2 fetch route resume because it crosses the active Mode Pack mutation boundary after approval.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive method is extended with one additional bounded journey_route_resume route kind and result metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds executable replacement route continuation, checkpoint validation, ledger evidence, and replay behavior rather than a report, digest, readiness, history, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates journey fingerprint, session sequence, route kind or replacement next action, selected-candidate approval checkpoint fingerprint, referenced provenance and fetch checkpoint consistency, registry-selection/current-active identity, replacement authorization, and replay identity; derives ModePackSelectedApprovedCandidateReplacementTarget; executes it through existing replacement continuation authority; persists bounded resume evidence; and replays without duplicate active replacement or candidate consumption.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can continue a Golden Journey from approved-candidate evidence into active Mode Pack replacement after a crash or boundary stop without reconstructing trusted replacement target identity in the caller.
answers.milestone_progress: Adds the active mutation route continuation needed before M50 can reach runtime-owned journey closure, uninterrupted Golden Journey completion, restart recovery, and finite Product DoD/Stop Evaluation.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.5 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime approved-candidate replacement route-resume phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one authorized bounded approved-candidate replacement journey-route resume envelope without adding a new RPC

the runtime derives modepack_selected_approved_candidate_replacement_target from persisted approval, provenance, fetch, registry-selection, and current active Mode Pack evidence instead of requiring caller-supplied replacement target construction

journey-route resume validates journey fingerprint, current session sequence, route kind or replacement next action, source approval checkpoint fingerprint, referenced checkpoint consistency, registry-selection/current-active identity, authorization, and replay identity before replacement side effects

unsupported route kind, missing authorization, stale checkpoint fingerprint, missing approval checkpoint, missing provenance or fetch checkpoint, checkpoint-evidence mismatch, current-active mismatch, and mixed explicit target requests fail closed without new replacement, drive, or resume evidence
replaying the same resume request returns committed bounded metadata without duplicating active replacement, candidate consumption, drive, or journey-route resume ledger evidence

resume result metadata contains bounded journey/task/run/session/drive handles, route kind, source checkpoint fingerprint, derived replacement target class, result advance/continuation id, post-route progress, next action, replay flag, and deterministic resume fingerprint

VSIX validators accept fetch, provenance, approval, and replacement bounded route-resume protocol shapes and reject malformed fingerprints, false authorization, mixed explicit targets, mismatched derived target classes, and raw/unbounded fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, new RPC, broad refactor, or VSIX-owned policy is added

Rust M50.1 journey admission tests continue covering journey admission denial, malformed journey ids, mixed admission targets, and conflicting replay boundaries

VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests accept valid fetch, provenance, approval, and replacement journey_route_resume params and journey_route_resume result metadata, reject mixed explicit targets, non-unit route budgets, malformed fingerprints, mismatched derived target class, and raw route-resume fields

FetchSelectedModePackCandidateExplicitly, VerifySelectedModePackCandidateProvenanceExplicitly, ApproveVerifiedModePackCandidateExplicitly, and ReplaceActiveWithApprovedModePackCandidateExplicitly are supported by route resume after M50.5
route resume cannot mix journey admission, caller-supplied explicit Mode Pack targets, context budgets, or completion finalization authorization

the source approval checkpoint fingerprint, referenced fetch/provenance checkpoint evidence, registry-selection/current-active identity, and current session sequence must match before replacement side effects

no additional route families beyond selected-candidate fetch, provenance verification, candidate approval, and approved-candidate replacement
no journey closure, automatic apply, recovery, verification retry, provider retry, parent join, shell, git, network, or service expansion
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or capability summary surface
rejected_alternatives: caller-side replacement target construction as sufficient
generic route executor for all Mode Pack steps
mixing journey closure, restart recovery, apply, or Product DoD into the same phase
technical_debt: M50.5 supports fetch, provenance, approval, and active replacement route resume; runtime-owned closure, uninterrupted Golden Journey, and crash/restart Golden Journey remain open.
The runtime monolith and large behavior-test module remain maintainability risks; module splitting should follow stable behavior slices rather than block Golden Journey capability.
M50 closeout should introduce finite Product DoD and deterministic stop evaluation so valuable phases continue only when they close an unfinished required DoD item.
Cross-version durable checkpoint recovery remains a later compatibility concern for long-running journeys that span runtime upgrades.
next_capability_rationale: After M50.5 merges, the next distinct M50 phase should close the runtime-owned Golden Journey from bounded replacement evidence.
Do not add another wrapper around route state; keep moving finite Golden Journey boundaries from caller-owned orchestration into Rust-owned replay-safe continuation.
